players.comment: McCollum (calf) will miss at least four weeks, per Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network. The veteran combo guard has been diagnosed with a left calf strain, and he's in line to miss the next month or so. Once rookie first-rounder Kingston Flemings (back) is healthy, he'll have a long runway as Atlanta's top point guard. Aaron Wiggins remains worth holding in nearly all fantasy leagues as well.

Clarkson (foot) is out for Wednesday's game against Cleveland. The veteran guard is missing a fourth consecutive contest with plantar fasciitis in his right foot. Clarkson didn't practice Tuesday and lacks a timeline for his return.

McConnell (hamstring) was recalled from the G League's Noblesville Boom on Tuesday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports. After missing Indiana's past two games with left hamstring soreness, McConnell joined the club's G League affiliate for practice Tuesday. The veteran point guard can be considered questionable for Friday's game against Philadelphia until the Pacers provide an update on his progress.

Nance exited Monday's game against the Thunder due to a sore right ankle and he will not return, Tony East of Forbes.com reports. Nance will have three full days to rest his sore ankle before the Pacers' next game, although with Friday's matchup with the 76ers being the first of a back-to-back set, Nance may need to miss that one as well. Obi Toppin figures to pick up most of Nance's minutes while he's sidelined.

Powell has been diagnosed with a mild right hamstring strain and will be re-evaluated later this week. Powell sustained the hamstring injury in Friday's loss to the Wizards and is now set to miss at least the next two contests. With the veteran swingman on the shelf, Isaac Okoro, Buddy Hield, Tre Jones and Patrick Williams are all candidates for increased playing time.

Prince underwent arthroscopic right knee surgery Nov. 18 and will be re-evaluated in four weeks, Eric Vincent of ClutchPoints.com reports. Prince last appeared in a game for Detroit on Nov. 14 and is now set to miss an extended period as he recovers from knee surgery. However, the veteran forward's absence shouldn't significantly impact Detroit's rotation.

Grant was diagnosed with a grade 1 left calf strain and will be re-evaluated in two weeks. Grant suffered the injury during Thursday's 126-98 victory over Golden State. He will now be sidelined for at least two weeks, with the team expected to provide an update on his condition at that time. While Grant is on the shelf, Taylor Hendricks and Kris Murray are candidates for more minutes.

Schroder (hamstring) is out for Wednesday's game the Bulls. Schroder remains out indefinitely with a hamstring strain. With Charlotte already eliminated from knockout-round contention in the NBA Cup, it's possible the veteran's point guard's absence extends into mid-December.

Embiid (illness) is out for Wednesday's game against Miami, Ira Winderman of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports. With Embiid set to miss a second straight game due to illness after previously being listed as doubtful, Philadelphia will again need to cover his vacated minutes at center. His absence removes one of the 76ers' top offensive options and should leave added frontcourt work available to the likes of Jabari Walker, Dominick Barlow and Adem Bona.

LaVine (knee) is listed as out for Wednesday's game versus the Warriors. LaVine will miss his second game of the 2026-27 campaign. His next opportunity to play will come Sunday against the Timberwolves. In the meantime, Leaky Black, Emanuel Sharp and Malik Monk are candidates for more minutes, with one of those players expected to move into the starting lineup.

Nurkic (foot) has been cleared for on-court work and will be re-evaluated in one week. Nurkic continues to make progress in his recovery from a partial plantar plate tear of the second toe on his right foot, and getting cleared for on-court work is a big step in his rehab. There are still a few steps he'll need to clear before he makes his return to the floor, but once he's able to get through full-contact, 5-on-5 work, we'll know he's close.

Porzingis announced on his social media that he's stepping away from basketball. Porzingis said he was looking forward to joining the Warriors, but his body didn't respond the way he wanted it too during his ramp-up process before the season. Additionally, he said he will work with the Warriors on a solution that "makes sense." Porzingis is making this decision to prioritize his health and will hopefully turn a corner soon on that front.

Allen (concussion) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against Chicago. Allen will miss a fourth consecutive contest due to a concussion. With the veteran swingman sidelined, Sion James (thigh), Grant Williams and Royce O'Neale are candidates for increased playing time. Allen's next chance to play will come Saturday against Brooklyn.
Landale (hip) won't play Sunday against the Pistons. This will be Landale's fourth consecutive game on the inactive list. His next chance to play will come Friday in Boston.

Wagner (knee) will not return to Wednesday's game against the Bucks, C.J. Holmes of the New York Daily News reports. Wagner played just four minutes prior to leaving the contest due to left knee soreness. He scored two points (0-1 FG, 0-1 3Pt) after sinking both free throws. Grant Nelson will get more minutes off the Nets' bench for the remainder of the game.

Robinson (quadriceps) is considered day-to-day as he progresses in his rehab, Eric Vincent of ClutchPoints.com reports. Robinson will miss a fifth consecutive contest Tuesday due to a left quadriceps strain, though he can be considered questionable for Friday's game against Milwaukee until the Pistons provide an update on his status. Kevin Huerter will likely continue seeing increased playing time for as long as Robinson is sidelined.

Simmons underwent successful surgery Tuesday to repair a torn right Achilles tendon, James Ham of ESPN 1320 Sacramento reports. Simmons had a quality preseason, averaging 10.5 points, 4.0 rebounds and 4.0 assists over 17.4 minutes per contest (two games). The 30-year-old was on track to suit up for the Kings on opening night, though those plans were halted after he suffered a torn Achilles tendon during practice. Now, Simmons will focus on rehab. However, it's unknown what the future holds regarding his career in the NBA.

Murray (ankle) is out for Friday's game against Memphis. This was the expectation after the star guard requested a trade from the Pelicans earlier Friday. Given his standing with the club, Murray can be tentatively considered doubtful for future contests while New Orleans tries to find him another home.

Brown (hamstring) will receive imaging, and the Sixers will provide an update Thursday, Ky Carlin of USA Today reports. Brown will get imaging on his troublesome left hamstring that he reaggravated in the second quarter of Wednesday's 111-104 win over Miami. He recently missed two games with the ailment, and it sounds like he could be in jeopardy of another stint on the sidelines. While Brown is out, Dean Wade is the top candidate to join the starting unit, while Kentavious Caldwell-Pope and Anfernee Simons are likely to see an increase in playing time off the bench.

DiVincenzo (Achilles) has been cleared for team basketball activities and is targeting a return to game action in January, Jon Krawczynski of The Athletic reports. DiVincenzo suffered a ruptured right Achilles in late April but is seemingly ahead of schedule in his recovery. With the veteran guard and Anthony Edwards (knee) both sidelined, Bones Hyland and Terrence Shannon figure to continue seeing increased playing time.

Anunoby (calf) participated in on-court work for the first time since sustaining the injury, Ian Begley of SportsNet New York reports. Anunoby has missed New York's last two games due to soreness in his left calf, and he's slated to miss his third consecutive regular-season outing Wednesday against Cleveland. However, this is a positive sign for the 29-year-old, and the Knicks will continue to provide updates on his status when they are available. Anunoby's next chance to take the court will come Friday versus Miami.

Curry (abdomen) will be re-evaluated Friday after Thanksgiving, Anthony Slater of ESPN.com reports. Curry has missed six consecutive games, including Wednesday's tilt versus Sacramento, due to an oblique abdominal tear he sustained against the Rockets on Nov. 11. The Warriors will provide further updates following the holiday. Golden State has gone 1-4 with Curry sidelined, so hopefully Friday will bear some positive news for the 38-year-old.

Isaac (knee) is out for Sunday's game against the Wizards. Isaac continues to deal with a knee injury that has kept him out of action for the entire 2026-27 season. He should continue to be considered week to week until the Magic offer an update on his recovery process.

Fox (shin) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against Portland, Jeff McDonald of the San Antonio Express-News reports. Fox will miss consecutive games for the first time in 2026-27. He's dealing with a right shin contusion, and his next chance to suit up will come Friday against the Lakers. Stephon Castle will continue running the Spurs' offense while Jordan McLaughlin gets additional run in the second unit.

Markkanen has been diagnosed with a non-displaced fracture in his right hand and will be sidelined for at least one month, Shams Charania of ESPN reports. Markkanen has missed two straight games due to what was being described as a right wrist sprain, but it appears the issue was much worse than initially thought. The talented big man now joins Jusuf Nurkic (foot) and Jaren Jackson (knee) on Utah's long-term injury list, while Keyonte George's status moving forward is unclear while dealing with an ankle sprain. Given all of the injuries, Ace Bailey and Darryn Peterson will have to lead the offense, while Isaiah Collier, Brice Sensabaugh, Svi Mykhailiuk, Josh Okogie and Josh Green are candidates for increased roles.

Reaves (heel) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Daniel Starkand of LakersNation.com reports. Reaves has missed the last five games with a left heel contusion but is trending in the right direction ahead of Friday's game at San Antonio. The Lakers will provide an update on his status by Thursday night, and the 28-year-old shooting guard's return would leave fewer minutes available for Quentin Grimes, Collin Sexton and Jake LaRavia.

Jackson has been diagnosed with a torn MCL in his right knee and will be sidelined for 6-to-8 weeks, per Shams Charania of ESPN. Jackson sustained the injury early in Monday's loss to Memphis, and he's now expected to miss at least a month and a half of action. The star big man's absence creates a major void in the Utah lineup, one that is likely to be filled by a timeshare of Jaxson Hayes (shoulder), Kyle Filipowski and Mo Bamba. The Jazz could also shift Lauri Markkanen (wrist), when healthy, to the center spot at times, perhaps allowing Ace Bailey to spend more time at power forward.

Head coach Micah Nori said Morant met with a doctor in Los Angeles, who gave him a positive outlook on his recovery from the hamstring injury. While Nori declined to update Morant's timetable, he added Morant "may not be out for as long as we thought," Trail Blazers Insider Sean Highkin reports. Morant was initially given a four-week timetable after he suffered a Grade 2 left hamstring strain on Oct. 30. It sounds like he's making solid progress, though it would be surprising to see him beat that timetable given the tricky nature of hamstring injuries. Scoot Henderson will continue to start in his absence and there will be more minutes available for Jrue Holiday.

Robinson (illness) is out for Tuesday's game against Washington, Taylor Snow of the Celtics' official site reports. With Robinson set to miss a third contest due to an illness, Boston will again be without one of its primary center options. His absence should continue to leave more frontcourt minutes available for Neemias Queta and Luka Garza on Tuesday, with the former being in line to see the lion's share of the playing time.

Barrett has been diagnosed with a right hamstring strain and will be re-evaluated in two weeks, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports. Based on his re-evaluation timeline, Barrett likely won't return to game action until mid-December at the earliest. Jamison Battle, Allen Graves and Jamal Shead are candidates for increased playing time in Barrett's absence, especially while Kawhi Leonard (knee) is also sidelined.

Miller underwent surgery Wednesday to repair a torn left rotator cuff and will be re-evaluated in six months, per Law Murray of The Athletic. It's a tough break for Miller, who had an opportunity to battle for a reserve role during training camp in the fall. The timeline for a return is likely to keep him on the shelf until after the All-Star break. Miller's extended stay on the sidelines gives Kobe Sanders a chance to crack the Clippers' rotation.

Nesmith is out for Monday's game against the Thunder due to right foot soreness. The swingman is sitting out the second leg of this back-to-back set and is likely facing a short-term absence. Nesmith's absence should get Obi Toppin onto the streaming map in fantasy leagues Monday.

Haliburton (hamstring) was recalled from the G League's Noblesville Boom on Tuesday, Tony East of Forbes.com reports. Haliburton joined the Pacers' G League affiliate for practice Tuesday, taking a significant step forward in his recovery from a left hamstring strain. However, Shams Charania of ESPN reported Friday that the star point guard is expected to miss at least two more weeks, so Haliburton isn't expected to return to game action in the near future.

Hayes (knee) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Lakers. Hayes left Sunday's tilt against the Mavericks with what's now being described as a left knee strain, and it's not yet known how much time he may miss beyond Monday. Mo Bamba should start at center for the Jazz and is worthy of streaming consideration in all fantasy leagues.

Smith (illness) is listed as out for Wednesday's game against Charlotte. Smith is dealing with a gastrointestinal illness, so he won't suit up Wednesday versus the Hornets. Without him, Nic Claxton will presumably enter the starting lineup. Zach Collins might also be more involved.

Castleton totaled five points (2-4 FG, 1-1 3Pt) and four rebounds in seven minutes during Tuesday's 132-116 preseason win over the Cavaliers. Castleton squeezed five points and four boards into his brief appearance, including a successful three-point attempt. The reserve center made productive use of his late-game opportunity, though his limited playing time leaves his regular-season role uncertain.

Watford (ankle) is out for Saturday's game against the Spurs. Watford can be considered week-to-week at this point until the Pelicans offer an update on his recovery. He hasn't played since Nov. 8 and is averaging just 7.2 points and 3.5 boards per game in his six appearances off the bench.

Pippen (back) is out for Wednesday's game against the Clippers. Pippen hasn't been available for Memphis since Oct. 29 due to a lumbar disc herniation and remains without a clear timeline to return. He can be deemed week-to-week going forward, though his absence could extend into mid-December if the Grizzlies don't advance in the NBA Cup.

McBride (adductor) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Cavaliers. McBride will miss his second consecutive contest despite participating in Tuesday's practice. With Jordan Clarkson (foot) also sidelined, Tyler Kolek and other reserve guards could see additional opportunities in New York's backcourt.

Mobley will receive treatment and participate in rehab after the team confirmed a diagnosis of a right great toe sprain, and he'll be re-evaluated in the next 7-to-10 days. Mobley is set to miss his third straight game Monday since suffering the injury, and he's slated to miss at least the next week while on the mend. The Cavs should have a better idea on when he'll return to the court as he begins to progress through the treatment and rehab phase.

Cunningham (knee) is listed as out for Tuesday's game against Orlando. Cunningham was listed as probable, so his absence for Tuesday's meeting with the Magic is concerning. Head coach J.B. Bickerstaff indicated that the knee has been giving the two-time All-Star some trouble of late, and while he's mostly played through it, he will now miss his second game of the 2026-27 campaign. Without Cunningham, Isaiah Joe will enter the starting lineup.

Moody (knee) is progressing toward a potential return between December and January after rupturing his left patellar tendon in March, Anthony Slater of ESPN reports. Moody has been limited to individual court work, but team sources indicate he's ahead of Jimmy Butler (knee) in the rehabilitation process and is expected to return before the veteran forward. The 24-year-old still has several recovery checkpoints to complete, and Golden State has not established an official timetable. His eventual return would help replenish a Warriors wing rotation that will open the season without both Moody and Butler.

The Wizards announced Monday that Beekman sustained a right acromioclavicular joint injury and will be re-evaluated in approximately three weeks. Beekman is set for an extended absence, with his re-evaluation timeline suggesting he could remain sidelined beyond the initial three-week window. The injury further limits Washington's backcourt depth, though Beekman's absence is unlikely to have a significant impact on standard fantasy leagues.

Clark (hamstring) has been ruled out for the next two weeks. Clark suffered a right hamstring strain during Saturday's 117-106 loss to Chicago. He played three minutes as a result of the injury, and he's now slated to miss at least two weeks and will be re-evaluated at that time. Terrence Shannon Jr. and Bones Hyland will see increased playing time off the bench in Clark's absence.

Banchero is expected to be sidelined for the next four-to-six weeks due to a right high-ankle sprain, Shams Charania of ESPN reports. Banchero left during Friday's loss against the Timberwolves due to an ankle injury, and follow-up tests have confirmed a high-ankle sprain for the fifth-year forward. With an extended absence expected, the Magic will have to rely more heavily on Franz Wagner and Desmond Bane offensively, and Tristan da Silva figures to be the top candidate to enter the Magic's starting lineup for as long as Banchero is sidelined.

Bittle (foot) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Bucks, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports. Bittle continues to work his way back from a fractured right foot, as he's yet to make his 2026-27 season debut. He remains week-to-week until Toronto provides a definitive update.

Ball (ankle) did not return to Wednesday's 113-106 win over the Thunder. Ball finished with 19 points (7-18 FG, 5-9 3Pt), seven rebounds, eight assists and one steal in 29 minutes. Minnesota won a third consecutive game, but we'll have to wait and see the severity of the ankle injury. If Ball misses time, Terrence Shannon Jr. and Bones Hyland would likely absorb most of the vacated minutes.

Williams (back) is listed as out for Wednesday's game against Minnesota. Williams has only played twice in the Thunder's last 11 games. It's unclear when he will be available to return, though his next opportunity to suit up will come Saturday in Milwaukee. With Aday Mara (shin) also ruled out, Kenrich Williams and Micah Peavy should both see more action versus the Timberwolves.

Champagnie (foot) is expected to miss several months, per Josh Robbins of The Athletic. The forward underwent surgery Wednesday to address a fractured foot, and the Wizards hope Champagnie will be ready to return at some time around the All-Star break in February. The likes of Bilal Coulibaly, Tre Johnson and Bub Carrington will all be asked to help pick up the slack for the foreseeable future.

Head coach Rick Carlise confirmed Sheppard will miss "months" after undergoing surgery to repair a torn meniscus in his left knee, Tony East of Forbes.com reports. Sheppard required a full repair and is without a definitive timetable for a return to action. With Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring) expected to miss at least two weeks, Quenton Jackson figures to see a significant uptick in playing time. Two-way player Braden Smith could also see increased action with the parent club.

Holmgren underwent a biological treatment Friday to address a small patellar tendon tear and will miss at least 8-10 weeks, Nick Crain of Slam reports. This is another massive blow to an Oklahoma City squad that's already set to be without Jalen Williams (leg) and Cason Wallace (shoulder) for most, if not all, of the season. With Holmgren sidelined, Kenrich Williams, Jaylin Williams and Aday Mara are all candidates to see increased playing time. Two-way player Brooks Barnhizer could also see more minutes.

Detroit recalled Duren (hamstring) from the G League's Motor City Cruise on Wednesday. Duren has been dealing with a hamstring strain since October, and his return is not yet expected in immediate contests. The fact that he has practiced with the G League club is still a good sign as he makes progress in his recovery. Duren would be a reliable source of production once he's healthy, but until then, John Collins and Paul Reed may continue to absorb his responsibilities at center.

Kalkbrenner (hip) has been ruled out for Wednesday's matchup with Chicago. Kalkbrenner exited Monday's loss to Memphis early with left hip soreness and is now set to miss Wednesday's contest. His next chance to play will come Saturday against the Nets. With the big man sidelined, Hannes Steinbach could see meaningful playing time behind Moussa Diabate.

Krejci underwent surgery on his fractured left ankle Wednesday and will be re-evaluated in eight weeks, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports. Krejci suffered the ankle injury in last Wednesday's win over the Suns and is set to miss an extended period after undergoing surgery. With the 26-year-old and Ja Morant (hamstring) both on the shelf, Jrue Holiday and Sidy Cissoko should continue seeing increased minutes.

Williams (ankle) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Pacers, according to the NBA's official injury report. Williams remains sidelined following left ankle surgery, with no confirmed return date. His continued absence leaves Oklahoma City without a key offensive contributor, allowing additional opportunities for the Thunder's remaining perimeter players.

Edwards underwent a successful arthroscopic procedure on his right knee Thursday, the Timberwolves announced. Edwards underwent debridement surgery in Minnesota, though the team did not provide a timetable for his return. The star guard is expected to make a full recovery, with additional updates coming as he progresses through rehabilitation. Based on previous reporting from ESPN's Shams Charania, Edwards could miss up to two months. Edwards was off to a scorching start this season, averaging 33.3 points, 4.8 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 2.0 steals across four appearances.

Edey (ankle) did not return to Wednesday's 115-97 win over the Clippers. He finished with seven points (3-4 FG, 1-1 FT), four rebounds, two assists and two blocks across nine minutes. Edey didn't return after checking out in the second quarter due to ankle soreness. Considering he's had two procedures on the same ankle since June 2025, the team will likely be overly cautious before allowing him to suit up. For now, Edey should be considered at least questionable for Friday's game against Minnesota. If he is ruled out for that contest, Isaiah Stewart and Taylor Hendricks are expected to see more minutes, with one of those players in line to start.

The Wizards announced Thursday that Watkins has undergone surgery for a torn ACL. Watkins, a two-way player for the Wizards, suffered the injury during the Summer League. Although Washington has yet to offer a timetable for a return, a typical recovery time for the procedure is approximately 9-to-12 months. That leaves Watkins in serious jeopardy of missing most, if not all, of the 2026-27 season, and it remains to be seen if the team will continue keeping him around on a two-way roster spot while he's injured.

Mathurin (foot) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Thunder. Mathurin will miss a fourth straight contest due to plantar fasciitis in his left foot, which tends to be a lingering injury. Jordan Poole should remain in the backcourt rotation for the undermanned Pelicans moving forward, while Mathurin can be deemed week-to-week.

Head coach Dusty May said Friday that Lively (foot) is moving well and progressing in his recovery, and the big man told May he's "close" to returning, Mike Curtis of The Dallas Morning News reports. Lively hasn't seen game action since Nov. 21, 2025, and he remains without a firm timetable to return after undergoing right foot surgery last December. However, this update suggests that the big man is trending in the right direction.

Wallace underwent surgery Friday to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder and will be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Clemente Almanza of USA Today reports. Wallace is expected to miss most, if not all, of the season. However, there's still a chance he will return late in the campaign after sustaining the shoulder injury in Sunday's win over the Clippers. With Jalen Williams (leg) also set to be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Alex Caruso (ankle) should see significant playing time once cleared to return. In the meantime, Jared McCain, Bennett Stirtz and Josh Dix are expected to see increased burn.

The Pelicans transferred Reese from the G League's Laketown Squadron, and he will be available for New Orleans' game against the Warriors on Monday. Reese dropped a 15-point, 15-rebound double-double in the Squadron's win over the Mexico City Capitanes on Saturday and will return to the parent club ahead of its game Monday. Through five regular-season appearances at the NBA level this season, the big man is averaging 1.2 points and 1.0 rebounds in 5.4 minutes per tilt.

Williams underwent surgery Thursday to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder and will miss an extended period of time, Shams Charania of ESPN reports. This is a tough blow for the center with training camp right around the corner. With his status for Opening Night in jeopardy, this will put a lot of eyes on Oso Ighodaro and Khaman Maluach, with the latter already drawing buzz during the Summer League. More clarity on Williams' timeline should be known in the coming weeks.

Youngblood (heel) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Knicks. Youngblood has been on the shelf since Nov. 10 due to a right heel bone bruise. Until Portland signals otherwise, Youngblood can be considered out indefinitely moving forward.

Gueye (foot) is ready to begin on-court activities and will be re-evaluated in four weeks, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports. The team stated in July that the big man would remain sidelined for the next 3-to-4 months after undergoing surgery to repair a fractured left foot, and he's continuing to make progress in his rehab. A timetable for Gueye's 2026-27 debut has yet to be established, thought a date could come into focus following his next evaluation in mid-December.

Hukporti has sustained a season-ending ruptured right Achilles tendon, per Shams Charania of ESPN. Hukporti went down with an Achilles injury in Monday's preseason opener against the Knicks, and an MRI has since revealed a rupture. He signed a one-year deal with the 76ers over the summer, so Hukporti will be an unrestricted free agent come season's end. With Hukporti's year already finished, Adem Bona (foot) should assume the backup center role behind Joel Embiid once healthy.

Newell underwent surgery Tuesday for a plantar plate tear in his left great toe, and he will be re-evaluated in approximately four months, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports. Newell suffered the toe injury in the Nov. 4 win over Washington and is now set to miss an extended period. With Mouhamed Gueye (foot) expected to miss at least three more weeks, Aaron Wiggins and Corey Kispert could see a slight bump in minutes moving forward.

Raynaud (knee) was recalled from the G League's Stockton Kings on Wednesday, Marc J. Spears of ESPN.com reports. Raynaud presumably joined the G League Kings for practice Wednesday. He's recovering from a right patellar subluxation and remains without a timetable to return, and while it's encouraging that he's getting reps with Stockton, the big man can be considered week-to-week until the Kings offer another update on his status.

Sharpe suffered a torn meniscus in his knee and is expected to miss six months, per Shams Charania of ESPN. It's a tough blow to the Trail Blazers' depth on the wing ahead of training camp. Sharpe, who is now likely to be sidelined until after the All-Star break, had been ticketed for a reserve role behind Toumani Camara following an injury-plagued 2025-26 campaign, which saw average a career-high 20.8 points, 1.4 steals and 2.1 three-pointers per game over 50 regular-season appearances. The door is now open for Vit Krejci and Jeremy Sochan to compete for bench minutes during camp.

Vukcevic (hip) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against Boston. Vukcevic has yet to suit up this season due to a left hip injury. He can be considered week-to-week until the Wizards provide an update on his progress.

Harper (hip) is expected to miss two to three weeks, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports. Harper has been diagnosed with a left hip external rotator strain, and San Antonio is now set to be without one of its regular guards for an extended stretch. His absence creates more backcourt minutes for the Spurs, likely most prominently for Justin Champagnie while the team waits for Tobias Harris (calf) to make his season debut. De'Aaron Fox and Stephon Castle should see extra ball-handling duties as well.

Boozer (ankle) will be re-evaluated in four weeks, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports. The rookie standout has been diagnosed with a moderate-grade ankle sprain, and he'll be sidelined for at least the next month or so. It's a tough blow for an upstart Grizzlies team, which will now rely even more heavily on Ty Jerome's playmaking for the foreseeable future. Taylor Hendricks has a chance to nail down a consistent role off the bench as well.

Knueppel (hamstring) was diagnosed with a left hamstring strain Sunday and will be re-evaluated in four weeks. Knueppel missed the first eight games of the 2026-27 campaign. He returned for the 114-104 loss to Brooklyn on Wednesday, though he exited the contest after just six minutes of work and didn't return. With Knueppel out of commission for at least a month, Grayson Allen and Sion James are candidates to replace him in the starting lineup, especially with Dennis Schroder (hamstring) sidelined for a minimum of two weeks.

Sorber underwent an arthroscopic knee procedure Tuesday to address inflammation at the patellofemoral joint in his right knee, and he's expected to return to on-court activities in 6-8 weeks, Steve McGehee of News 9 Oklahoma City reports. Once Sorber begins on-court work, there will be a ramp-up period before he's cleared for game-time action, so his absence will likely extend well beyond this initial 6-8-week window. Sorber was selected by the Thunder with the No. 15 pick in the 2025 NBA Draft, but he missed his entire rookie season after tearing the ACL in his right knee and has yet to play this season due to right knee issues.

Wilson (hand) is expected to miss four to six weeks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports. The rookie forward went down during Wednesday's loss to the Spurs, and he now needs surgery to repair a fractured right hand. More pressure will likely fall on Josh Giddey going forward, while the likes of Tre Jones and Isaac Okoro will have a chance for added streaming value.

Quaintance has been around the team but has not yet been cleared for basketball activities, Matt Guzman of SI.com reports. The Spurs are expected to exercise extreme caution with the big man, as Quaintance suffered a torn ACL and meniscus with Arizona State in February 2025 before appearing in only four games with Kentucky last season due to severe complications and persistent swelling. The 19-year-old underwent a cleanup procedure on his meniscus in mid-July, and the Spurs will likely want him at 100 percent before ramping him up to basketball activities.

Saunders signed a two-way contract with the Grizzlies on Saturday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports. Saunders is still on the mend from a torn right ACL that he suffered during his final year at BYU. However, he has been cleared for on-court activities and will be allowed to practice with the Grizzlies now that he's officially signed with the team.

Jackson underwent a procedure Wednesday to repair a broken fifth metatarsal in his left foot. He is expected to recover fully and will be re-evaluated in approximately three months. Jackson suffered a foot injury in Saturday's 129-110 win over the Nets. Head coach Tuomas Iisalo indicated after the game that the injury was "relatively serious," though it is now confirmed he will miss extended time. While Jackson is out of commission, Taylor Hendricks and Jerami Grant should receive more playing time.

Veesaar was diagnosed with a torn right ACL and is expected to miss the 2026-27 season, the Hawks announced Monday. Veesaar suffered the injury during a workout on Sept. 15, and an MRI confirmed the diagnosis. The No. 52 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, Veesaar was expected to spend a lot of time with Atlanta's G League affiliate this season.
Lawal (groin) is out for Tuesday's game against Denver. Lawal is slated for a fourth consecutive absence due to a right groin strain. His next opportunity to return will arrive Friday in Phoenix.

Tomlin (back) will remain on the inactive list for Wednesday's game against the Grizzlies. Tomlin, who is recovering from a lower back stress reaction, has yet to suit up for the Cavs this season. He continues to get ruled out 24 hours in advance of tipoff, indicating he's still not close, so he can be viewed as week-to-week moving forward.

Head coach Sean Sweeney said Wednesday that Nelson (ankle) has been doing "some on-court stuff," though Sweeney added that the work has been "minimal," Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports. Nelson underwent surgery this offseason to repair a fractured left ankle. It's encouraging to hear that he's made some progress, but the two-way player can still be considered week-to-week moving forward.

Biberovic (heel) is out for Wednesday's game against the Warriors. Biberovic has yet to debut for the Mavs this season due to a right heel bursitis issue, and the fact that he continues to get ruled out a full day in advance of tipoff suggests he's still not close. Biberovic should be considered week-to-week moving forward.

Topic (hip) is listed as out for Wednesday's game versus Minnesota. Topic has appeared in only three games for the Thunder this season. He's missed the last three contests because of a hip strain, with his next opportunity to suit up coming Saturday in Milwaukee. Without Topic, Bennett Stirtz and Josh Dix could continue to receive more playing time.

Mara (leg) is out for Wednesday's game versus the Timberwolves. This will be Mara's third straight game on the inactive list, and for now, he should be considered questionable at best for Saturday's game in Milwaukee. With Jaylin Williams (back) also unavailable, Micah Peavy and Kenrich Williams will help back up Isaiah Hartenstein at the center position.

Penda (hamstring) is making progress but remains without a timetable to return to game action, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports. Penda suffered a partially torn hamstring in the preseason and can still be considered week-to-week moving forward. With the second-year forward and Paolo Banchero (ankle) both sidelined, Tristan da Silva and Jamal Cain should continue seeing increased minutes.

The Pistons announced Tuesday that Okorie (oblique) will miss at least two weeks, per Eric Vincent of ClutchPoints.com. Okorie has been diagnosed with an oblique strain, which he sustained in a G League game. The rookie first-rounder has logged a grand total of 20 minutes across five brief appearances, so his absence doesn't have major fantasy ramifications.

De Larrea (knee) is listed as out for Wednesday's game against the Warriors. De Larrea has only played four games during the 2026-27 campaign. There hasn't been any indication of when he will be cleared to return, so he should be considered week-to-week for now.

Traore will be re-evaluated in approximately 8-10 weeks due to a right hamstring strain, Michael Scotto of HoopsHype.com reports. Traore had a productive start to his second year in the NBA, though he's now set to miss an extended period after sustaining a hamstring injury in Friday's loss to Orlando. With the 20-year-old point guard sidelined, Egor Demin, Mikel Brown and Keon Ellis are candidates for increased playing time.

Butler (knee) could return sometime between January and February as he continues recovering from a torn right ACL, Anthony Slater of ESPN reports. Butler, who underwent surgery after suffering the injury Jan. 19, has progressed to individual court work but still has several rehabilitation milestones to clear. His next step involves landing comfortably after a game-speed jump. Coach Steve Kerr is hopeful Butler can rejoin Golden State for the latter portion of the season, though no official return date has been announced. The 37-year-old forward remains a significant part of the Warriors' plans and could provide a substantial boost during the second half of the campaign.

Harris (calf) is likely to be sidelined until early December, per Jeff Garcia of KENS 5 San Antonio. Chris Haynes of NBA TV reported Friday that Harris is expected to ramp up his activity this week, and that the veteran forward could make his season debut as soon as early December. Until Harris is finally cleared to return from a calf strain, Julian Champagnie should continue to handle an expanded role on the wing.

Leonard has begun individual on-court workouts following treatment to address swelling in his left knee, and he will be re-evaluated in one week, Marc J. Spears of ESPN.com reports. Leonard continues to progress in his recovery, and the Raptors are expected to provide another update in a week. Collin Murray-Boyles and Allen Graves will likely continue seeing increased burn for as long as Leonard is sidelined.

Beal (knee) will not be ready for the start of the regular season, NBA writer Justin Russo reports. Beal is dealing with knee inflammation that will keep him sidelined for Opening Night. While it's unclear how long the Clippers will be without the veteran guard, Darius Garland, Keaton Wagler and Kris Dunn should dominate the backcourt minutes in his absence. Beal's 2025-26 campaign was cut short by a hip injury after he averaged 8.2 points and 1.7 assists in 20.6 minutes across just six regular-season appearances.

Drummond (head) did not return to Wednesday's 121-102 win over the Cavaliers. Drummond played nine minutes off New York's bench, finishing with three points (1-1 FG, 1-1 3Pt) and two rebounds. Pacome Dadiet, Tyler Nickel and James Wiseman could all see a boost in playing time if Drummond is forced to miss any time. His next chance to suit up will come against the Heat on Friday.
